newsitem.title: GERMANY: European budget deficits still too high - Buba.
newsitem.headline: European budget deficits still too high - Buba.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday that budget deficits in most European countries remained too high, placing a restriction on growth in the private sector.

Noting that European countries "with the exception of Germany" had made progress in reducing their budget deficits last year, the central bank nonetheless hit out at attempts by some countries to effect only temporary improvements.

"'Balance sheet cosmetics' clearly do not help in the task of consolidation," the central bank said. "They neither create new fiscal policy scope nor strengthen the competitiveness of the private sector," it said in its 1996 annual report.
Sustainability would be essential for those countries entering monetary union, it said.

Convincing policies, including overall stability policies, would also be important for those countries which have already benefited from convergence trading on bond markets, which has reduced their long-term interest rates, it added.
Convergence trading refers to the reduction in bond yields resulting from market expectations that a country will be able to qualify for European monetary union.

"The countries concerned must concentrate convincingly on a long-term stability policy in order to prevent considerable setbacks in interest rate and exchange rate developments which could occur in the event that expectations are disappointed," the Bundesbank said.

Such convergence trades have been driven by the expectation that European monetary union will start on time in 1999 with a large group of countries, the Bundesbank said, making no comment on the likelihood of this scenario.

Looking generally at countries' readiness to join EMU, the fiercely-independent German central bank noted that many countries still had to give more freedom to their central banks in advance of the start of EMU.
